main_text.p: enim spreverant nuper optima & fidis-sima ipsius monita, & soli è Græcis injuriosè de eo locuti fuerant. Verum is posthabitis contumeliis cum in castra venisset, pro obsessis intercessit apud consulem, & obsidione solutà inducias iis confecit tanti temporis, per quod Romam legatos deprecatores mittere, iiqué cum responso in patriam redire possent. Profectis verò Romam legatis, & in senatu auditis, post multam actionem tandem tale responsum datum: oportere Ætolos aut senatus arbitrio libero sese permittere, aut mille talenta pendere, & simul eosdem amicos velinimicos cum Romanis habere: nec impetrari à petentibus potuit, ut quasi rerum arbitrium permitti sibi posset, senatus profiteretur. Iussi autem legati sunt eodem illo die urbe, intra dies xv Italiâ excedere. Succensebant quippe Ætolis Romani vehementius quàm indomitæ genti, qui odio Romani nominis Antiochum nuper in Europam exciverant, & vastationum & cædium innumerarum causam dederant. Inter quos Acilius consul XLIII principes Ætolicæ gentis, & in his [?]ocritum illum, qui castra in Italiâ se sisturum, atque iis Quinctio se responsurum jactaverat, ejusdemque fratrem in

page.notes: Printed text is set in a slightly blurred scan; the name at the start of the "in his" clause is partly hidden under a stain and is only partly legible, so it is marked [?]. The left margin carries fragmentary marks (e.g. "si", "ʃ", "p", "g") that are too damaged to transcribe as notes. Last word of the page is cut off at the right edge and continues on the next page. Long s is shown as plain s throughout, as the rules require.
